r: **By Parliament in 1972** (assent 9 Sept 1972); first comprehensive wildlife law
**Wild animals, birds and plants** and their habitats
Illegal hunting of wild animals – barred by the Act
"Animal" = amphibians, birds, mammals, reptiles, their young, eggs of birds and reptiles
Hunting of scheduled animals **prohibited**, subject to exceptions
Animal **dangerous to human life** (or crops), or diseased or disabled beyond recovery, may be captured / killed with the Chief Wildlife Warden's permission
Permits for education, research, scientific management, translocation
**Teasing, molesting, injuring or feeding** animals in a zoo prohibited
Wild animals = **State Government property**; in a Centre-declared sanctuary / NP = Central Government
Tiger Conservation Plan for every TR (2006)
Centre may notify a non-Schedule I animal as vermin
Cannot be hunted by anyone except as the law permits
Equal inside or outside PAs; mere *apprehension* of danger is not enough to kill a protected animal
When it endangers human life, and when it is diseased (two separate grounds)
Barred inside NPs and sanctuaries; SC bars mining within **1 km** of every NP / sanctuary unless a larger ESZ is notified
I and II: absolute protection (tiger, rhino)
V: **vermin** (common crow, fruit bats, rats, mice)
VI: **specified plants** – cultivation only with a **licence**
6 in the 1972 Act; 4 since the 2022 amendment (in force 1 April 2023)
A tortoise in Schedule I gets **the same protection as the tiger**
**Licence required to cultivate**; a specified plant cannot be picked, uprooted or traded without permission
A **fruit bat** (Pteropus); does not feed on blood; was **vermin (Schedule V)**, since 2022 in **Schedule II**
Asiatic lion, tiger, elephant, snow leopard, rhino, Gangetic dolphin, dugong, GIB, **blackbuck**
**6 → 4**; vermin schedule deleted (Sec 62 power stays with the **Central Government**)
Centre regulates **invasive alien species** (African catfish, Lantana)
Voluntary **surrender of captive animals without compensation**; Chief Wildlife Warden in every State; Centre may notify conservation reserves
Specially protected animals – minimum **₹25,000** (from ₹10,000); general violations – maximum **₹1 lakh** (from ₹25,000)
**NBWL** replaced the Indian Board for Wildlife; **Conservation Reserves** (government land, e.g. **Tsarap Chu**) and **Community Reserves** (private / community land)
A **reserved forest** assigned to a village community
Everything banned unless permitted; **Sec 26** = acts prohibited, incl. punishable **trespass**
Activities allowed unless prohibited – **head-loads of wood**, produce for own use, **cattle grazing**
Outside the reserved and protected categories
**Bamboo grown outside forest areas** removed from the definition of "tree" (**Sec 2(7)**) – may be felled and moved without permit; bamboo **inside** forests is not freed
British policy encouraged **monocropping through plantations** (tea, coffee, teak) – a cause of environmental degradation
**Prior approval of the Central Government (MoEF)** to de-reserve a forest or use forest land for **non-forest purposes**
Land notified as forest under IFA 1927 or any law, and land **recorded as forest on or after 25 Oct 1980**
Strategic linear projects within **100 km** of IB/LoC/LAC; zoos, safaris, eco-tourism
Equal non-forest land, else **twice** the degraded forest land + **NPV**
"Forest" = every area recorded as forest **irrespective of ownership**; the 2023 amendment narrows this
Set up June **2007**; HQ **New Delhi**; **five regional offices**: Delhi, Kolkata, Mumbai, Chennai, Jabalpur
Statutory advisory body under the **Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act 1960**, set up **1962**; HQ shifted from **Chennai** to **Ballabhgarh (Faridabad, Haryana) in 2018**
Afforestation and wasteland development; reforestation in existing forests; **wood substitutes and alternative fuels**
Forest Policy, EPA 1986, Industrial and Educational Policy all relate to it

r: Wild animals, birds, plants and habitats
Umbrella law – **protection and improvement of the environment**
Cruelty to animals; parent Act of AWBI
**NBA (Chennai, 2003)**, State Biodiversity Boards, **Biodiversity Management Committees** (prepare **People's Biodiversity Registers**)

Offences **decriminalised** (civil penalties); exemption for AYUSH practitioners and **BMC-certified** cultivated medicinal plants; NBA approval **180 → 90 days**; foreign entities **still need** prior NBA approval
Forests (**Entry 17A**) and wild animals and birds (**Entry 17B**) to the Concurrent List; inserted **Art 48A** (DPSP) and **Art 51A(g)** (Fundamental Duty)
Needs the **President's assent** because it amends a **central law** (Maharashtra 2026, Sec 12; leopard **Schedule I → II**)
Wildlife sanctuary, national park, conservation reserve, community reserve, tiger reserve
Private / community land; declared by the **State Government**
**Hunting not allowed**; people may **collect non-timber forest produce**; **traditional agriculture (jhum) not allowed**
NP – no grazing, no human activity except as the Chief Wildlife Warden permits; sanctuary – regulated grazing
